name: Downtown and Jellybean Row
tagline: The painted houses above the harbour
description: The tiers of brightly painted row houses climbing from the harbour, with Water Street and Duckworth Street holding the restaurants, the shops and George Street's bars a block off. It is the most photographed part of the city and the most walkable.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to walk everywhere and be in the middle of it
pros: The painted row houses and harbour views
Best restaurants and pubs in the province
cons: Loud at night near George Street
The hills are punishing in ice

name: Georgestown
tagline: The residential slope east of downtown
description: A hillside neighbourhood of narrow streets and older houses just east of the centre, quieter than downtown and closer to Signal Hill. The Rooms and Bannerman Park sit at its edges, and the walk into town takes about ten minutes downhill.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting quiet within walking distance of downtown
pros: Ten minutes on foot to downtown
Bannerman Park and The Rooms nearby

name: Quidi Vidi
tagline: The fishing village inside the city
description: A tiny harbour tucked behind the hills northeast of downtown, still working, with a brewery in the old fish plant and a handful of houses around the gut. The lake behind it hosts the Royal St John's Regatta, the oldest sporting event in North America.
bestFor: Anyone wanting a village setting inside a capital city
pros: A working fishing harbour in the city
Quidi Vidi Brewery and the lake trail
Coastal trail access from the gut
cons: A drive or long walk from downtown
Exposed and windy on the harbour

name: Rabbittown
tagline: The affordable grid north of the centre
description: A working residential neighbourhood on the slope north of downtown, ordinary houses on a tight grid with corner shops and the cheapest rents within walking distance of the centre. It is where most people who live in St John's rather than visit it actually are.
bestFor: Budget stays within walking distance of downtown
pros: Twenty minutes on foot to downtown
cons: Nothing much to walk to locally

name: Churchill Square and the University
tagline: The campus side with the shops and the newer flats
description: The area around Memorial University and Churchill Square, with the largest concentration of newer apartments, a good run of shops and cafes around the square, and Long Pond and the Rennie's River trail below the campus.
bestFor: Anyone wanting newer housing and the university nearby
pros: The newest apartment stock in the city
Rennie's River trail and Long Pond
cons: Fifteen minutes from downtown by car
Student turnover in the rental market
Less character than the older districts
